item.title: Las aseguradoras rozan el 6% del patrimonio en planes de pensiones individuales
item.description: El patrimonio bajo gestión de los planes de pensiones del sistema individual ha aumentado un 5,11% en los nueve primeros trimestres, situándose el total gestionado en 93.517 millones de euros, según Vdos. Los grupos independientes registran el mayor incremento patrimonial, con un 9,6%, seguido de las aseguradoras, que crecen un 8,27% , y grupos internacionales (7,38%). En todo caso, los bancos mantienen su posición mayoritaria de cuota de mercado con un 76%, seguido de grupos independientes y las aseguradoras, con un 8,42% y un 5,95%, respectivamente.

item.title: LA Wildfire Smoke Exposed 7 Million to Dangerous Toxic Metals
item.description: A catastrophic 2025 Los Angeles firestorm exposed some 7 million people to high levels of airborne lead and other toxic metals released from burning homes and vehicles, according to a new study. Scientists for the first time were able to quantify in real time the chemical composition of wildfire smoke thanks to a sensor network that went online months before the January 2025 Eaton conflagration that destroyed more than 9,400 buildings, killing 19 people. As climate change triggers urban firestorms like the inferno in the LA suburb of Altadena, the paper published Wednesday in the journal Science Advances offers the first indication of how the incineration of homes, electronics, cars and infrastructure could affect even people who live far from the burn zone due to wind-blown toxic smoke.

Insurers cannot future-proof their claims operations as long as supplements remain a digital afterthought, which is why Cotality has officially launched a powerful supplement management platform that brings structure to intake, routing, review and reporting. item.title: FCA stops HTX's crypto promotions
item.description: The FCA has secured High Court undertakings to ensure that HTX (formerly Huobi), a global crypto exchange, will not knowingly promote cryptoasset services unlawfully to UK consumers. Steve Smart, executive director of enforcement and market oversight at the FCA, said: 'Crypto firms should be under no illusion: being based overseas does not put them beyond the reach of UK law. The FCA took legal action against HTX in October 2025 for breaking UK financial promotion rules.

item.title: What does 'fair value' look like in practice? Three years into the Consumer Duty, here’s what we’ve learned.
item.description: Three years into the Consumer Duty, we’re seeing clear differences between firms that have embedded fair value into their approach and those that still need to strengthen their assessments, evidence and monitoring. Fair value is a simple yet important principle at the heart of the Consumer Duty : the price customers pay should be reasonable, relative to the benefits they get. We recently reviewed how firms across the consumer finance market assess, evidence and monitor fair value.

item.title: Jumbo Series A Rounds Hiding The Real Squeeze On Seed Startups
item.description: Global startups have closed at least 114 Series A rounds of $100 million or more so far this year, Crunchbase reported in late September, and more than 70% of them went to AI companies. startups closed 272 Series A rounds in the third quarter, according to Crunchbase data, about 28% fewer than the 377 a year earlier. Uncork Capital ‘s Andy McLoughlin told Crunchbase News that Series A investors now expect $2 million to $3 million in ARR, sometimes $4 million, and the time from seed to A has stretched past two years.

item.title: Series B Funding Is Up, But Fewer Deals Are Getting Done
item.description: Series B startup funding in 2026, as venture capital investment continues to concentrate heavily around a handful of AI hotshots. The smallest Series B deals have gotten particularly scarce. Nuclear energy startup Valar Atomics also secured $1 billion in Series B funding across tranches this year, with Sequoia Capital as lead investor.

item.title: GAM Swiss Re Cat Bond fund strategy launched in New Zealand as PIE Fund
item.description: The GAM Swiss Re Cat Bond investment fund strategy will now be available to investors in New Zealand in the tax efficient Portfolio Investment Entities format, as the GAM Swiss Re ILS Income NZ PIE Fund opens for business on November 6th. The PIE strategy will invest substantially all of its assets in the NZD hedged share class of the GAM Swiss Re Cat Bond, which is the long-standing Irish-domiciled UCITS cat bond fund that was launched in 2011. The GAM Swiss Re ILS Income NZ PIE Fund launches as a fund strategy sitting within the GAM Investment Funds PIE Scheme and is designed to provide New Zealand investors with an efficient route to access the returns of a global portfolio of insurance-linked securities (ILS), primarily catastrophe bonds, in an NZD-hedged format.

item.title: ILS funds upward trajectory continued in September, with 1.55% return: ILS Advisers Index
item.description: Insurance-linked securities investment fund strategies, across catastrophe bonds and private ILS, delivered another strong month of returns in September 2026 with their upward momentum continuing, as the average ILS fund performance reached 1.55%, the latest data from the ILS Advisers Fund Index shows. September’s reporting is already based on 100% of constituent ILS funds in the Index, with the 1.55% average return the second-highest monthly performance for the sector only to the now updated August figure. “Against this benign catastrophe backdrop, ILS investments continued their upward trajectory, delivering another strong month of performance,” ILS Advisers said.

item.title: Hamilton aims to upsize Easton Re catastrophe bond to $300m at lower pricing
item.description: Hamilton Insurance Group, the Bermuda based insurance and reinsurance holding company, returned to the catastrophe bond market earlier this month with an initial target to secure $250 million of protection from this Easton Re 2027-1 offering . This 2027-1 issuance is set to be the third 144A catastrophe bond offering under the Easton Re name for Hamilton’s reinsurance entity Hamilton Re , while the company has also sponsored a private cat bond prior to those deals. It’s good to see Hamilton looking to build on its catastrophe bond protection even more, while the decline in pricing is no surprise given how cat bond issues have been executing of late with the market well-capitalised and fund managers having cash to deploy.

item.title: Hippo and Greenlight Re establish partnership to support emerging MGAs
item.description: has partnered with Greenlight Capital Re’s Innovations segment, which links investment opportunities in emerging MGAs with carrier and reinsurance support, allowing Hippo to co-invest with Greenlight Re in early-stage programs while its subsidiary, Spinnaker Insurance Company, can serve as Greenlight’s preferred U.S. “The partnership builds on those existing relationships to establish a more coordinated approach to evaluating emerging programs and accelerating speed to market with full insurance stack capabilities,” Hippo explained. “It supports our strategy to grow across insurance products while applying the underwriting discipline that has shaped Hippo’s business — the same discipline that helped build many of our biggest program partners today.” Jesse Willmott, president, reinsurance and portfolio management at Spinnaker Insurance Company, said, “This partnership combines Greenlight Re’s track record of making significant investments in emerging businesses, and Spinnaker’s track record of quickly bringing programs to market with the right underwriting capabilities and capacity.

item.title: Heritage’s net income rises to $51.1m in Q3’26 despite higher cat losses
item.description: Heritage Insurance Holdings, Inc., a super-regional property and casualty insurance holding company, reported net income of $51.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, up 1.4% from $50.4 million in the prior-year quarter, despite $15.8 million in pre-tax catastrophe losses, compared with none in the prior-year quarter. Total revenue amounted to $219.2 million, up 3.2% from $212.5 million, reflecting higher net premiums earned and increased investment income. Heritage’s net combined ratio was relatively flat at 73.0% compared with 72.9%.

item.title: Pacific Life Re announces protection leadership changes across global markets
item.description: Pacific Life Re, an international life reinsurance company providing reinsurance solutions and support to life insurers, has announced changes to the leadership of its global Protection business. Pacific Life Re said the changes will bring pricing and underwriting functions together under a single global leadership structure, alongside dedicated leadership for key regional markets. “By bringing leadership closer to clients and markets, we are strengthening our ability to support their ambitions while continuing to provide access to the global capabilities, expertise, and support that help them succeed.” As part of the revised structure, Pacific Life Re has appointed Jia Yi Tan as chief pricing, underwriting and claims officer, Protection.

item.title: New Data Centers Projected to Emit More Carbon Than All of Mexico
item.description: The environmental nonprofit Union of Concerned Scientists in January projected that fossil-fuel-powered electricity for data centers could increase US power-sector emissions by 19% to 29% , or as much as 342 million tons a year by 2035. If the rush to build AI data centers leads to the upper bounds of the emissions projected by these researchers, it represents a reversal of a two-decade economic and policy trend toward less US power-sector climate pollution. The surge in construction of fossil-fueled power plants to run AI data centers is set to undo 15 years’ worth of greenhouse gas reductions from US electricity generation, according to an internal analysis by the Sierra Club.

item.title: Three Bodies Recovered in Gabon Following Sinking of Borr Drilling Rig
item.description: Three bodies were recovered in Gabon on Wednesday following the sinking at the weekend of Borr Drilling’s Prospector 5 rig off the coast of the southern town of Mayumba, the Central African country’s navy said. The rig is contracted to support BW Energy’s drilling operations off Gabon and it had not yet begun drilling. Chief of Staff of the Gabonese Navy, Charles Hubert Bekale-Meyong, said three bodies were found on Wednesday and two people were still missing.

item.title: Barclays Turns to Insurers to Hedge Billions of Data Center Debt
item.description: As the AI-buildout accelerates, credit risk insurers have taken on greater exposure to data center finance, according to a survey from Willis Towers Watson Plc released in May. Barclays Plc is looking to buy default protection on more than $10 billion of debt to finance artificial intelligence infrastructure in a bid to create capacity for more lending as hyperscaler funding needs soar. Several providers of so-called non-trade credit risk insurance had indicated that they were “approaching sector limits or are already full on data center exposure,” according to the Willis survey.

item.title: More Rain for Flood-weary U.S. Southwest Expected
item.description: Yet more flooding made parts of the normally arid Four Corners region look more like an ocean than a desert Monday as locals kept a wary eye on a forecast for still more rain ahead. With parts of his town of 250 underwater, Mayor Josh Ewing was worried by a forecast for yet more heavy rain this weekend. After a few days of sunny, dry weather, more rounds of rain are predicted Friday night and again on Sunday, according to the National Weather Service.

item.title: JAB Insurance completes acquisition of Utmost Life and Pensions
item.description: JAB Insurance has completed its acquisition of Utmost Life and Pensions from Utmost Group plc, marking its entry into the UK insurance market. Anant Bhalla, Senior Partner & CIO of JAB Holding and Executive Chairman of JAB Insurance, said: "Today we welcome the Utmost Life and Pensions business and all its policyholders into the JAB Insurance family. We look forward to working closely with Andrew and his team to support JAB Pensions’ ongoing growth, continue servicing policyholders and pension scheme members, and provide greater choice for pension risk solutions in the UK." Andrew Stoker, Chief Executive Officer of Utmost Life and Pensions, said: "Getting to know Anant and the JAB Insurance team throughout this process has reinforced my confidence in where we're headed together – their experience and genuine focus on pension scheme members and insurance policyholders came through at every stage.

item.title: PNC Bank to embed ADP Payroll and insurance solutions
item.description: The offering, PNC Payroll by ADP, will provide access to payroll, HR, benefits, time tracking, insurance and retirement solutions alongside PNC’s banking, payments and cash management capabilities. PNC Bank and ADP have announced a partnership to bring payroll and workforce services into PNC’s digital banking platform for small businesses. It will combine digital self-service tools and AI-enabled payroll and HR capabilities with 24/7 access to ADP payroll experts.

item.title: esure offers car insurance quotes through ChatGPT
item.description: UK insurer esure has a ChatGPT app that allows users to request car insurance quotes through the platform. Car insurance offered through the app is arranged and administered by esure Services Limited and underwritten by esure Insurance Limited. esure Insurance Limited acts as the data controller for motor insurance quotes and policy purchases, while esure Services Limited handles product sales and distribution.

item.title: PolicyMe launches AI underwriting copilot
item.description: Canadian insurance distributor PolicyMe has launched an internally developed AI copilot to help underwriters review life insurance applications. The copilot consolidates medical records, lab results, and supporting documents into one workspace, generates structured case summaries, and suggests underwriting decisions with supporting evidence. PolicyMe says most applicants already receive decisions in seconds through its automated underwriting technology.

item.title: U.S. Regulator Proposes Incorporating NFPA Rules to Speed Up LNG Projects
item.description: A US regulator proposed new rules on Wednesday to hasten liquefied natural gas projects and expand export capacity as part of the Trump administration’s larger push to speed up energy infrastructure development and cut costs for consumers. He ordered the resumption of LNG export approvals – something former President Joe Biden had paused – and also started to streamline the environmental approval process that previously slowed projects. The proposed rulemaking updates PHMSA’s safety framework for LNG facilities by incorporating National Fire Protection Association standards for the siting, design, construction, operation, and maintenance of LNG facilities.

item.title: TikTok Videos, Lack of Safeguards Could Push Increased Theft Threat for Certain Cars Through 2050
item.description: Using models and data from the Los Angeles Police Department, Brantingham and his colleagues predict the surge in thefts will continue in Los Angeles through at least 2042, and likely through 2050. Engine immobilizers are standard anti-theft equipment in most cars; without them, theft is a relatively “low-skilled” crime. YouTube and TikTok videos soon emerged — tagged “Kia Boys” or “Kia Challenge” — that amplified the criminal activity and provided step-by-step instructions on how to carry out the thefts, the researchers said.

item.title: Exclusive: Numeracle Raises $28M To Keep Legitimate Business Calls From Spam Label
item.description: Numeracle has raised $28 million from Edison Partners to help businesses whose calls are incorrectly labeled as spam or blocked by phone carriers, it tells Crunchbase News exclusively. The company also plans to adapt its business verification tools for use beyond phone calls. Numeracle charges an annual subscription to monitor and address incorrect spam labels.

item.title: VIG Re seeks €50m Euro wind retro with debut Charles Bridge Re cat bond sponsorship
item.description: VIG Re, the reinsurance arm of Vienna Insurance Group, is the latest first-time sponsor to enter the catastrophe bond market, as the company seeks a €50 million or greater source of fully-collateralized European windstorm retrocession through a Charles Bridge Re 2026 DAC issuance, Artemis has learned. Charles Bridge Re 2026 DAC has been established in Ireland as a designated activity company for VIG Re’s debut catastrophe bond, sources have told us. The structure is set to offer and sell a single tranche of notes to cat bond investors, with the proceeds of this sale to be used to fully-collateralize a retrocessional reinsurance agreement between Charles Bridge Re 2026 DAC and VIG Re.

item.title: Scale of client needs requires us to connect risk with capital beyond traditional: Aon CEO Case
item.description: “Traditional insurance capital remains critically important, but the scale of emerging client needs increasingly requires us to connect risk with capital beyond the traditional insurance market. Aon’s CEO Greg Case explained today that the scale of emerging client needs means the broker has to look beyond the traditional insurance and reinsurance market for capital, such as in the recent example of a partnership with an alternative asset manager. “Our ability to quantify risk exposure and provide investors with the insight required to deploy capital with confidence will create additional capacity for clients and expand the universe of insurable risks.” Case also said in response to a question that “ the evolution of bringing capital into the industry is here before us because of client need.

item.title: Evolving ILS capital landscape an opportunity. Broker facilities no threat: RenRe CEO O’Donnell
item.description: RenaissanceRe CEO Kevin O’Donnell explained during the firm’s third-quarter earnings call today that the evolution of the insurance-linked securities capital landscape is an opportunity for the reinsurance company, while he also commented on broker facilities saying that he sees them as disintermediating smaller players in the market. Ultimately, much of this capital will want to have someone come in to accumulate the risk on their behalf.” Moving to respond to the question on broker facilities, which remains a hot-topic given recent activity such as Aon’s partnership with Blackstone on the Cortina structure, O’Donnell highlighted that he does not see these ventures as a threat to RenaissanceRe’s business. O’Donnell responded to a question asking how RenaissanceRe views the entry of new investors into reinsurance in support of the growing number of sidecar structures, including casualty ILS structures, as well as more direct routes to access risk such as broker facilities.

item.title: QIC gross premiums grew 9% to QR 8.5bn in 9M’26
item.description: Qatar Insurance Company (QIC) has reported gross written premiums of QR 8.5 billion for the first nine months of 2026, a 9% increase from the same period a year earlier. QIC said the increase in gross written premiums was underpinned by selective growth across its domestic, regional and international portfolios, achieved while maintaining underwriting discipline in a softening global reinsurance market. Disciplined underwriting and a high-quality investment portfolio have allowed us to absorb the impact on our insurance service result and higher claims costs while continuing to grow insurance revenue, Gross Written Premium and investment income.

item.title: EverPeak appoints Patrick Daley as CUO
item.description: EverPeak Insurance, a United States-based workers’ compensation insurer, has appointed Patrick Daley as its new Chief Underwriting Officer (CUO). In his new role, Daley will lead underwriting strategy and quality standards across all EverPeak lines of business. Kathy Kranz, President, EverPeak, commented on the appointment, “Patrick has built his career on underwriting the risks that demand real judgment, discipline, and creativity.

item.title: Property cat rate declines to slow at Jan 1, supply of capital now much more disciplined: RenRe CUO
item.description: Global reinsurer RenaissanceRe (RenRe) expects property catastrophe rate declines to decelerate at the January 1 renewals, and also anticipates the market will remain disciplined with respect to terms and conditions and structures, noting that the supply of capital willing to accept risk is much more disciplined than it was a decade ago. So, the supply of capital willing to accept risk has been much more disciplined than what we might have seen 10 years ago, where flexibility of structures was more of the key,” explained Marra. In his prepared remarks, Marra said that ahead of the key January 1 renewals, RenRe expects the property market to remain competitive but attractive, with healthy demand likely to be outstripped by supply.

item.title: Texas Volunteer Firefighter Charged With Arson
item.description: A Central Texas volunteer firefighter faces 16 felony arson charges after investigators say he set grass, vehicle, and structure fires in Moore and Pearsall. Winchester is a firefighter with the Moore Volunteer Fire Department The fires caused significant damage to vegetation, fences, vehicles, and structures. The SFMO is working with the Frio County Sheriff’s Office, the 81 Judicial District Criminal Interdiction Task Force, Texas Game Wardens, and Pearsall ISD Police Department on the investigation.

item.title: People Moves: Bg I of Illinois Names Leming as President
item.description: Chris Leming, senior vice president of TROXELL in Springfield, Illinois, has been named President of Big I Illinois. As President, Chris is responsible for leading the direction of Big I Illinois over the next year and will act as an official delegate of the association at state and national functions. In his volunteer role for Big I Illinois, he has served as Regional Director, Government Relations Committee Member, Vice President, and President-Elect.

item.title: DOJ Recovers $604K in Back Wages from Indiana Auto Parts Manufacturer
item.description: Department of Labor has recovered $604,000 in back wages for 829 workers after an investigation found an Indianapolis-area vehicle parts manufacturer failed to properly calculate overtime wages. Toa (USA) LLC, with manufacturing facilities in Mooresville, is the primary body structure and suspension components supplier for Subaru of Indiana Automotive and Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing North America. Investigators with the department’s Wage and Hour Division found that Toa (USA) LLC, a major automotive supplier that serves top-tier automotive companies, did not include a non-discretionary attendance bonus for hourly employees when calculating overtime during applicable workweeks, in violation of the overtime provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act.

item.title: Ethos and Liberty Mutual expand life insurance partnership
item.description: Under the expanded partnership, Liberty Mutual's life insurance offering powered by Ethos is now available online and through Liberty Mutual call centres. The expansion takes the partnership beyond its April 2026 starting point, adding new sales channels for the life product and linking Ethos life cover with savings on Liberty Mutual's auto and home insurance. In addition, eligible customers now receive savings on Liberty Mutual auto and home insurance when they hold an Ethos life policy.

item.title: Verisk brings insurance content to Amazon Quick and Microsoft Copilot and expands its offering within Claude
item.description: The post Verisk brings insurance content to Amazon Quick and Microsoft Copilot and expands its offering within Claude appeared first on Insurtech Insights . With the new integrations, Verisk's insurance content is now available across three AI platforms: Amazon Quick, Microsoft Copilot, and Claude. Verisk has launched new integrations that bring its ISO Loss Costs and PAAS content to Amazon Quick and Microsoft Copilot.

item.title: Mapfre reports €924m net profit for the first nine months of 2026
item.description: Mapfre has reported net profit of €924m for the first nine months of 2026, up 11.5%, with premiums above €22.8bn, up 2.0%. The figures cover the nine months to 30 September 2026. Reinsurance unit Mapfre Re reported net profit of €286m, up 11.8%, with a combined ratio of 95.3%.

item.title: Why the Surge in Business Interruption Claims?
item.description: Business interruption claims now average 70% more than property damage losses as concentrated production and fragile supply chains amplify risk. New claims analysis from Allianz Commercial shows that the average total value of a business interruption claim now exceeds €850,000. Allianz's report analyzes 7,888 business interruption insurance industry claims with a total value of approximately €6.74bn, or US$7.82bn, from Jan.

item.title: Avante raises $30 million Series A
item.description: Avante , an AI platform for employee benefits teams, raised $30 million in Series A funding led by Frist Cressey Ventures, with participation from new investors Sorenson Capital, Hearst Ventures, and Morgan Stanley Next Level Fund, alongside existing investor FUSE. The round brings its total funding to $40 million. Avante says it has signed more than 70 customers in the 18 months since launch, including several Fortune 500 and Global 2000 companies, and supports more than 385,000 employees and family members.

item.title: TempusDirect secures investment from Aldrich Capital Partners
item.description: TempusDirect , a provider of medical claims cost containment services for P&C insurers, has received a strategic investment from private equity firm Aldrich Capital Partners. Founded in 2016 and based in Tempe, Arizona, TempusDirect helps insurers review medical bills, negotiate payments with healthcare providers, and evaluate medical expenses included in attorney demand packages. The company plans to use the investment to expand product development, client services, and business development, while adding automation across its offerings.

item.title: WTW to acquire ARESS brokerage business in Colombia
item.description: WTW has agreed to acquire the insurance brokerage business of Colombia’s ARESS Corredores de Seguros. Founded in Medellín in 1967, ARESS specializes in risk management, insurance brokerage and consulting. Margarita López, WTW’s Colombia country head, pointed to ARESS’s risk management expertise and longstanding client relationships as key reasons for the transaction.

item.title: El Banco Central de Perú aclara los límites contractuales de los adquirentes, pero expertos prevén retos en cláusulas de permanencia
item.description: El Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCRP) dictó una norma para regular el servicio de aceptación de pagos que prohíbe cláusulas que restrinjan a los comercios la contratación de otros aceptadores de pagos. La norma, que entrará en vigor el 1 de enero de 2027, tampoco permite establecer tarifas o descuentos especiales que incentiven el uso exclusivo de un solo aceptador. 0026-2026-BCRP, el regulador busca que exista libertad para elegir con cuáles proveedores trabajar, mientras deja un margen de negociación acotado para los aceptadores.

item.title: Celia Castañs (Tributos) sustituye a Jorge Alberto Ferreras en el Consejo del Consorcio
item.description: El Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa ha nombrado a Celia Castañs García , subdirectora general de Tributación de las Operaciones Financieras de la Dirección General de Tributos, como vocal del Consejo de Administración del Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros, en sustitución de Jorge Alberto Ferreras Gutiérrez , cuyo cese también se ha publicado en el BOE. Por su parte, Ferreras fue nombrado en marzo de este año director general de Tributos del Ministerio de Hacienda. Castañs fue nombrada subdirectora general de Tributación de las Operaciones Financieras el pasado mes de septiembre, después de ejercer como coordinadora de área en el mismo departamento.

item.title: Sabseg compra la correduría MecVis en su objetivo de ser líder del middle market italiano
item.description: Como adelantó su CEO, Eduardo Dávila , en la entrevista concedida a las publicaciones de INESE a principios de año, Sabseg tiene al mercado italiano en su foco de crecimiento para este año dentro de su objetivo de convertirse en el bróker de referencia en el mercado de intermediación de seguros del Sur de Europa, con más de 2.000 millones de primas intermediadas, antes de 2030 . De esta forma, tras las incorporaciones de Asigest, Today e Insurance Solutions, se sabe ya su cuarta compra en el mercado transalpino: la correduría Mec.Vis S.r.l., especializada en el asesoramiento y la gestión de riesgos empresariales . La operación le permite a Sabseg ampliar su presencia en el noreste de Italia, con implantación en Trentino-Alto Adigio y nuevas oportunidades de desarrollo en el Véneto .
